data.description: I was at the pickup point at Tiong Bahru Plaza on time but the driver never showed up. I waited 10 minutes at the lobby and couldn't find the car. The app charged me a $5.00 cancellation fee for a 'no-show' which is completely unfair — I was there, the driver was not. I want the charge reversed immediately.

I'm waiting at the lobby area, white Honda HR-V plate [plate redacted].
Outgoing call to rider — not answered (rang 22s, no response).

data.details: Rider R-7823 booked trip TRIP-2026-09945 from Tiong Bahru Plaza to VivoCity. Scheduled pickup 08:45.
Driver D-2398 ([name redacted], Honda HR-V [plate redacted]) assigned. ETA 13 min.
Driver started navigating to pickup location. Live tracking enabled.
Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.
Push notification + in-app alert sent to rider: 'Your driver has arrived.'
Free wait timer started. 5 min free wait period ends at 08:48.
Driver initiated in-app call to rider. Call rang 22s, no answer.
Free 5-min wait period expired. Rider had not boarded. Cancellation fee now applicable per policy.

policyRules.text: The driver must wait at the pickup location for a free wait time of five minutes from the scheduled pickup time. After five minutes the driver may cancel for rider no-show.
The rider is charged a S$5 (500 cents) no-show cancellation fee when the driver cancels after the free wait period; the fee compensates the driver.

Before cancelling for no-show the driver must attempt at least one in-app chat message AND at least one phone call through the in-app calling system. Failure to satisfy both contact obligations voids the cancellation fee. An unanswered call is still an attempt; contact after cancellation does not qualify.

If the driver has not arrived by scheduled pickup plus five minutes, the rider may cancel without charge. If the driver fails to arrive AND fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a separate S$5 goodwill credit. That credit is a distinct action from refunding a fee.
A safety incident or safety-related allegation requires human review regardless of dispute category or amount.
For safety incidents, agents may gather and summarize evidence but cannot determine fault or recommend a resolution.

Dispute value under S$10 permits automatic determination at any confidence level; S$10 through S$50 requires confidence of at least 80%; above S$50 always requires human review. Category restrictions in §6.2 also apply.

Route deviation requires confidence of at least 80% AND deviation no greater than 2 km; otherwise human review. No-show/cancellation is eligible for automatic determination at its fixed S$5 fee. Safety always requires review.

findings.text: The driver arrived at the designated pickup point at 08:43:00, two minutes before the scheduled pickup time of 08:45:00, as recorded by GPS data and platform events.

The driver cancelled the trip after the free wait period had expired, making the S$5 no-show cancellation fee applicable as per policy rules RYDE-V2.1-2.1 and RYDE-V2.1-2.2.

data.description: The driver took a significantly longer route from Orchard Central to Changi Airport T3. I normally take the PIE which takes about 35 minutes and costs around $28. On this trip the driver went through Geylang and East Coast area, taking 37 minutes and the fare was $35. The driver did not inform me about any route change or traffic. The extra distance was 4.3 km and I was overcharged. I am requesting a refund of the excess fare.

data.message: Hi! I'm at the Orchard Central main entrance, wearing a blue dress. White Toyota Vios right?
Yes that's me! I can see you, coming now. 1 min.
Great thanks! Heading to Changi T3, my flight is at 3:30pm.
Sure, no problem. We will get there in time.
Hey, are we going the right way? This doesn't look like the usual route to the airport.
Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.

data.calculation: (actual kilometres - recommended kilometres) * distance rate; currency rounded to integer cents

policyRules.text: Rerouting for traffic, road closures or congestion is allowed, but the rider must be informed.
Before or at deviation the driver must inform the rider through in-app chat or verbally supported by the trip call recording, with a brief reason.

Deviation no greater than 1 km is within tolerance with no excess-distance refund. Above 1 km: traffic-justified and informed/agreed rerouting has no refund; traffic-justified but unnotified rerouting permits a partial refund of excess distance fare; unjustified rerouting requires the full excess distance fare refund. Category escalation in §6.2 still applies before an automatic ruling.

Deviation distance is actual route distance minus recommended route distance. Historical traffic evidence at the trip time verifies traffic justification. Chat or call evidence confirming acknowledgment establishes rider agreement.
A safety incident or safety-related allegation requires human review regardless of dispute category or amount.
For safety incidents, agents may gather and summarize evidence but cannot determine fault or recommend a resolution.

Dispute value under S$10 permits automatic determination at any confidence level; S$10 through S$50 requires confidence of at least 80%; above S$50 always requires human review. Category restrictions in §6.2 also apply.

Route deviation requires confidence of at least 80% AND deviation no greater than 2 km; otherwise human review. No-show/cancellation is eligible for automatic determination at its fixed S$5 fee. Safety always requires review.

driver_brief.position: The driver's route deviation was justified by active traffic incidents, and the record does not support a refund. The fee should stand.

claims.text: Historical traffic evidence shows a high-severity vehicle fire blocking lanes on the PIE eastbound, the recommended route, at the trip start time, verifying traffic justification for a reroute.
The driver's actual route taken, as verified by GPS telemetry, resulted in a trip duration of 37 minutes, which is close to the estimated 35 minutes for the recommended route.
The driver informed the rider through in-app chat that they knew the way and would reach the destination on time after the rider questioned the route.

adverseEvidence.text: The driver did not provide a brief reason for the route change in the in-app chat when the rider questioned it.
The actual route taken was 4.3 km longer than the recommended route distance, exceeding the 1 km tolerance.

concessions: The driver's chat response did not explicitly cite the traffic incident as the reason for the route change.

rider_brief.position: The supplied record does not establish a policy basis for reversal.

claims.text: The driver's route deviated 4.3 km from the recommended distance, exceeding the 1 km policy tolerance.
Verified traffic incidents on the recommended PIE route at the trip time justify rerouting for traffic.

adverseEvidence.text: The rider reports the driver did not inform them about the route change, but the driver's chat response does not acknowledge the rider's question or provide a traffic-related reason.
The verified excess distance fare is S$3.44, and the total fare delta is S$6.50.

concessions: The traffic incidents on the PIE route at the trip time provide a valid justification for avoiding that route.
unansweredQuestions: Did the driver verbally inform the rider of the rerouting due to traffic before or during the deviation, as no trip call recording or corresponding chat message is supplied?
What was the driver's specific intent for the route taken? The supplied GPS trace shows a route through Geylang and East Coast, but the driver's stated reason in chat is not traffic-specific.

rider_rebuttal.response: The driver advocate's claim that the driver 'informed' the rider by stating 'I know the way' does not meet the policy requirement to provide a brief reason for the deviation due to traffic.

claims.text: The rider questioned the route via in-app chat at 13:24, and the driver's response did not mention traffic, congestion, or a road closure as the reason for the route taken.
Policy §1.2 requires the driver to inform the rider, before or at deviation, with a brief reason, which the supplied chat record does not establish.

preservedConcessions: The traffic incidents on the PIE route at the trip time provide a valid justification for avoiding that route.

driver_rebuttal.response: The Rider Advocate correctly identifies that a traffic justification exists, but misapplies the policy by concluding the record does not support a refund. Under Rule 1.3, a traffic-justified but unnotified rerouting permits only a partial refund of the excess distance fare, not a full reversal. The driver's position that the fee should stand for the justified portion is the strongest supported outcome.

claims.text: Historical traffic evidence verifies a high-severity vehicle fire blocking the recommended PIE route at the trip start time, providing traffic justification for the reroute.
The policy states that for a traffic-justified but unnotified rerouting, the permitted remedy is a partial refund of the excess distance fare, not a full reversal of the fee.
